analysis: Frame 9 of the data set (two-storey two-bay frame, gravity loads only), units kip and inch. Plane frame in the global X-Y plane (Y vertical); the out-of-plane DOFs (uz, rx, ry) of every node are held (the data set's frames are 'fully braced out-of-plane'); in-plane bending about local z, so the data set's Izz is the section's Iz. Modulus 0.8 E = 23200 ksi (the data set's condition for all elastic analyses; its element table points to E = 29000 ksi, the published results correspond to 0.8 E - verified for this frame with the first-order displacements). No shear deformation. A straight line of the data set's elements is one member here, the loads at its interior nodes are point loads on the member. The data set's model is plane (no out-of-plane buckling of a member between joints); the engine's member is spatial, so Iy = 1000 Izz is entered for every section instead of the listed Iyy: no out-of-plane mode can precede the in-plane behaviour compared, and Iy does not enter the in-plane results. Linear buckling analysis on the PERFECT geometry with the loads as listed in the model file; target: the data set's elastic critical load ratio (MASTAN2 eigenvalue analysis, 4 elements per member with a polynomial geometric stiffness; 'lowest sway buckling mode'). The engine's members carry the exact stability functions.
